text:
Maya: Quick sync — kicking off the AcmeAnalytics onramp. Need cross-team alignment on launch criteria, security gating, infra capacity, and runtime changes. High-level product criteria: latency p95 < 200ms (text-gen), error rate < 1%, feature flag rollout, and SAML SSO + KMS for customer keys. Who's blocking?

Sam: Sam (eng-runtime) — latency target is achievable but we need to expose an adaptive batching config and tweak KV cache TTL per-tenant. I estimate 3d to land the patch + 2d for internal perf runs.

Olivia: Olivia (eng-infra) — we can reserve a canary pool: 4x A100 for 2 weeks. Need exact instance sizing (vCPU/mem) and expected qps. Also: are we doing canary in us-west only?

Maya: I'll own load tests. Expected steady qps ~200, burst ~600. Yes canary needs to be us-west for data residency.

Diego: Diego (security) — flagging this as high-risk because customer data includes PII. I need a dataflow diagram + list of PII fields and retention policy. Can you get that to me? I can do a threat model + checklist if I have the doc by EOD Tuesday.

Maya: Adding Elena for contract/SSO specifics. @Elena can you post the fields and SAML requirements?

Elena: Elena — shared a draft spec in the docs channel: https://internal/docs/acme-integration (mock link). PII fields: user_email, account_id, session_token. SSO: SAML2 with SP-initiated flow, customer requires attribute mapping on email + org_id.

Sam: Runtime notes: we'll add a feature flag `enable_adaptive_batching` and a per-tenant `kv_ttl_sec`. Suggested rollout policy example:
```yaml
rollout:
  canary: 5%
  ramp: [25%, 50%, 100%]
  monitors: [p95_latency, error_rate, tokens_per_sec]
  rollback_on: error_rate > 1% or p95_latency > 220ms
```
Infra needs to support autoscale steps and a fast restart window for node swaps.

Olivia: Infra can support the ramp. Two asks: 1) hot restart < 30s so autoscale doesnt overshoot; 2) we need the test harness to validate node lifecycle. If you give sizing by Fri we can provision on Mon of week2.

Diego: Security gating checklist (pre-launch): 
- Dataflow diagram 
- Threat model write-up 
- KMS key provisioning + key rotation policy 
- Audit logging enabled and routed to secure retention 
- SAML config validation with customer test tenant 
We can sign off once all items present and a quick pen test is scheduled.

Maya: Proposed timeline:
- Week 1: runtime patch + unit/integration tests (Sam)
- Week 1 end: infra sizing finalized (Olivia), contract artifacts (Elena)
- Week 2: provision canary in us-west + run load tests (Maya)
- Week 2 mid: security threat model + pen test kick-off (Diego)
- Week 3: ramp and monitor; rollback if thresholds hit
Does that align with capacity?

Sam: I can hit patch in week1, will need the test harness early (ideally Mon) to validate batching behavior.

Olivia: We can provision week2 Mon if sizing is final by Fri. Adding autoscale policy to infra checklist.

Diego: I can produce the threat model by Tue of week2 if I get current dataflow now. Will schedule pen test the moment we have a canary endpoint.

Elena: I'll export the schema + SAML assertions tomorrow EOD and attach a sample SAML metadata file.

Maya: Action items (short):
- Maya: run & own customer load tests + rollout coordination
- Sam: land runtime patch, provide testable flag + test plan
- Olivia: reserve nodes, implement autoscale ramp, confirm hot-restart times
- Diego: threat model, pen test scheduling, audit log requirements
- Elena: SAML config + PII schema + contract clauses
I'll drop a one-pager with the timeline and responsibilities after this thread.

deploy-bot: deploy status — no deploys scheduled for this thread :robot_face:

Sam: :eyes:

Olivia: :thumbsup:

Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the kickoff doc and a short Loom for the customer constraints.
